newsitem.title: JAPAN: Big Japanese firms show 15% rise in interim profit.
newsitem.headline: Big Japanese firms show 15% rise in interim profit.

text.p: Six-month earnings figures from more than 550 major Japanese firms showed an average increase in profit of nearly 15 percent, a corporate survey showed Monday.
Wako Research Institute of Economics said the parent current profits of firms increased by an average of 14.52 percent in the first half of the 1996/97 fiscal year.
Current profit is pre-tax profit that includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
The research arm of Wako Securities Co. based its figures on the interim parent current profit results of 565 firms. The list does not include banks, brokerages or insurance firms.
The parent current profits of car makers and auto parts manufacturers surged 152.97 percent, while those of real estate developers dropped by an average of 67.64 percent, the survey said.
